claimed_mechanism: The propagating chi mode is normalized by an independent standard kinetic term carried by the multiplier K, so its quadratic action does not inherit the screened preferred-frame factor. The preferred-frame response is isolated in a local khronon-chi coupling with alpha ~ e^-y but no lapse weight, preserving the transverse metric DOF. A spatially nonlocal chi operator supplies the DC-001 lensing channel while remaining local in time and active in the deep MOND limit. Matter remains minimally coupled to the single physical metric and mu(y)=1-e^-y is frozen.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate explicitly escapes DC-003 because every coupling is explicitly non-lapse-weighted; the MOND flux is not N-weighted and the metric potential is not identified with lnN, so the H_perp demotion and zero-quadratic-action disease are structurally absent. It is not a coefficient tweak of the rejected architecture: the preferred-frame term is retained but its lapse weight is removed, and a new spatially nonlocal chi coupling is added to carry the DC-001 lensing escape. It is inequivalent to constraint-first because chi and K have independent standard kinetic terms, to degenerate because the quadratic sector is nondegenerate, and to multi-sector because there is one physical metric with only auxiliary chi/K and a fixed khronon frame.
name: Nonlocal-Kinetic Screened-Frame Decoupling
predicted_weak_field: In the unscreened low-density limit e^-y is order unity, so the preferred-frame khronon term and the spatial nonlocal term both contribute to the MOND potential and lensing response. In the screened high-density limit e^-y suppresses the preferred-frame and nonlocal channels, while the K-normalized chi kinetic term stays finite and nondegenerate. Because no coupling carries a lapse weight, H_perp is not demoted and the quadratic action retains a finite propagating mode rather than collapsing to the Horava lambda=1 pathology.
